The app's Export step writes one folder per export group, with everything you
need to submit your records to GenBank: the sequences, their FASTA headers,
feature tables, and a summary of the checks. This page explains what each part
is for, and what to check before you upload. [Get started](RiboPilot.html)
shows the Export step itself.

# Which files to upload

For rRNA and ITS sequences, NCBI's Submission Portal
(https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov) takes a FASTA file only. Upload
`<group>.fasta`. The Portal finds the genes itself with ITSx, and writes its own
annotation, so the `.tbl` feature tables are not used there.

The `.tbl` files are for NCBI's command-line program
[table2asn](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genbank/table2asn/), the other route
into GenBank. Run it with `-V v`, read the `.val` report it writes, and send the
`.sqn` file the way NCBI's current instructions say.

The Portal rewrites definition lines in its own wording (small and large subunit
ribosomal RNA), so the 18S and 28S wording in your file will not survive that
route.

# The FASTA header template

Each record's FASTA header comes from a template. The default is:

```
{seqid} [organism={organism}] [moltype=genomic DNA] {organism} {rrna_definition}
```

and the default for the per-marker files is:

```
{seqid}_{element} [organism={organism}] {organism} {product}
```

Edit them in the **Export Data** window. Each template is checked as you type,
and **Save template** keeps it under a name, so a lab can keep one per
submission style. Words in braces are filled in for each record:

| Token | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `{seqid}` | The record's name: the sample ID, or `<ID>_p<path>_s<scaffold>` when the sample gives more than one record. Keep it in every template. |
| `{organism}` | The organism name to submit (see below). |
| `{rrna_definition}` | The definition phrase, for example "18S ribosomal RNA gene, partial sequence; internal transcribed spacer 1, 5.8S ribosomal RNA gene, and internal transcribed spacer 2, complete sequence; and 28S ribosomal RNA gene, partial sequence." |
| `{completeness}` | "complete sequence" or "partial sequence", for the record as a whole. |
| `{elements}` | The features in order, for example `18S-ITS1-5.8S-ITS2-28S`. |
| `{length}`, `{n_features}`, `{missing}` | Record length, number of features, and missing features. |
| `{sci_name}`, `{taxid}` | The name and NCBI taxon ID set in the Taxonomy step. |
| `{element}`, `{product}` | Per-marker template only: the marker (18S, ITS1, and so on) and its product name. |

Any column of your mapping file works too, as `{ColumnName}`. The **Available
columns** list in the Export Data window shows every name you can use.

# Required source modifiers

NCBI asks each rRNA or ITS record for the organism, one identifier for the
specimen (isolate, strain, clone, or specimen voucher), the collection date, and
where it was collected. Add them to your template as source modifiers, spelled
exactly as NCBI spells them. NCBI's page
[Modifiers for FASTA Definition Lines](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genbank/mods_fastadefline/)
(checked on 24 September 2026) spells them `[specimen-voucher=...]`,
`[collection-date=...]`, and `[geo-loc-name=...]`, with hyphens.

For example, with `Voucher`, `Date`, and `Country` columns in your mapping file:

```
{seqid} [organism={organism}] [specimen-voucher={Voucher}] [collection-date={Date}] [geo-loc-name={Country}] [moltype=genomic DNA] {organism} {rrna_definition}
```

If a record would get an empty modifier, such as `[collection-date=]` for a
sample with no date, the template check warns and names the records. NCBI does
not accept an empty modifier: fill in the column, or take the modifier out.

# The organism name

`{organism}` is the name confirmed in the Taxonomy step when your Taxon matched
it exactly, or when you picked a species there by hand. Otherwise it is your
Taxon label, as you typed it, so an informal name such as "Upeneus sp. A" is
kept. To always use your own label, put `{Taxon}` in the template instead.

When your Taxon differs from the name set in the Taxonomy step, the record's
`submission_risk` column says `taxon_differs(<name>)`, so you can check which
one you want.

# Samples with more than one record

When a sample gives more than one record, for example two rDNA variants from one
fish, RiboPilot adds `[isolate=<ID>_p<path>_s<scaffold>]` to each header. This
is on purpose: GenBank needs something to tell apart records that share an
organism and a voucher, and these labels let one sample send several records in
one submission. The values name records, not separate individuals. If GenBank
staff ask, tell them the records are different rDNA scaffolds from one specimen.

For that reason, a template with its own `[isolate=...]` is refused for an
export group that holds such a sample. It is allowed otherwise.

# Complete or partial

A gene end is written as partial (`<` for the 5' end or `>` for the 3' end in
the feature table, and "partial sequence" in the definition line) when:

- it runs into the end of the scaffold;
- the quality check found the gene truncated, meaning less than 90 percent of
  it was recovered. The end that meets no neighbouring spacer or gene is marked;
  if both ends meet one, both are marked; or
- you set it with the **5'** or **3'** button under **Partial** in the unit
  window (check **Edit**, pick the feature, then **Save**).

The quality check sets these marks once, after annotation. Your own choice is
kept when the unit is curated again. **Mark Partial** on the unit only changes
`{completeness}` to "partial sequence"; it does not mark any gene end.

# Flanking sequence

Records keep the sequence around the genes: part of the external spacer (ETS)
before the 18S and part of the intergenic spacer (IGS) after the 28S. RiboPilot
does not annotate these flanks. That is fine: GenBank annotates rRNA and ITS
submissions itself, and does not use RiboPilot's annotation.

# Gaps inside a record

For the table2asn route, each run of 10 or more N bases is written to the
feature table as an `assembly_gap`, with linkage evidence "unspecified".

# Check before you submit

**Flagged records.** Before it writes anything, the Export window lists every
unit that the BLAST screen or the chimera check flagged, and that you
have not marked Reviewed. **Leave them out** is the default; **Export anyway**
exports them with their flags in the summary. Lock asks about the same units
first, in the Assemble and Annotation Review steps. When the export is done, its
summary names every record that has a submission-risk flag, and why.

**The final ITSx check.** NCBI's Portal runs stock ITSx on every rRNA and ITS
submission, and may remove records it judges chimeric, gapped, or misassembled.
RiboPilot runs the same check on your records after writing them. The result is
in the `itsx_check` column of `<group>_summary.csv` and in
`<group>_itsx_check.csv`. It only warns: nothing is removed.

**The submission_risk column.** Each record's row in `<group>_summary.csv` lists
any of these flags:

| Flag | What it means |
|---|---|
| `chimeric(...)` | Parts of the sequence match different phyla or kingdoms (a severe chimera call); the reason is in brackets. |
| `chimeric(ITSx)` | ITSx calls the record chimeric. |
| `gap_in_rDNA` | A run of N bases falls between the start of the 18S and the end of the 28S. |
| `misassembly` | Features overlap or are out of order. |
| `off_target(<taxon>)` | The BLAST screen's hits agree on a taxon that is not on the sample's lineage. |
| `contaminant` | The BLAST screen's best hit is from a different phylum than the sample. |
| `taxon_differs(<name>)` | Your Taxon differs from the name set in the Taxonomy step. |
| `missing_organism` | The record has no organism name. |

Check `off_target` and `contaminant` records before you submit: the sequence may
be another organism's rDNA, exported under your sample's name. Weaker chimera
evidence is in the separate `chimera_warning` column; it is not a submission
risk, but it is worth a look in the app.

**What your marks do.** A unit is exported when its sample is locked in the
Assemble step, the unit is locked in the Annotation Review step, its scaffold is
kept, and it is not marked Exclude from export. The Export window lists each
unit of the group that is left out, and why.

| Mark | What it does to the export |
|---|---|
| **Mark Reviewed** | Lock and the Export window no longer ask about the unit's contamination or chimera flags. The summary's `reviewed` column says yes. |
| **Exclude from export** | The unit is left out of every export. |
| **Mark Partial** | `{completeness}` reads "partial sequence". Gene ends are set per feature (see above). |

# What is in the export folder

```
out/export/<group>/
    <group>.fasta           every record, one file (this is what you upload)
    <group>.tbl             feature tables (table2asn route only)
    <group>_summary.csv     one row per record, with the submission_risk column
    <group>_report.html     review report with feature maps and alignments
    <group>_itsx_check.csv  what stock ITSx says about each record
    README.txt              how to submit
    samples/                one .fasta and .tbl per record
    markers/                one folder per marker: 18S, ITS1, 58S, ITS2, 28S, ITS
    itsx_check/             raw ITSx output behind the check
```

The summary CSV also says which records are variants of each other, in the
`variant_class`, `variant_group`, `variant_identity`, and `n_variants` columns;
see [Quality checks and flags](Curation-Flags.html).
